newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Dadas plunges as investors bail out.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Dadas plunges as investors bail out.

text.p: Shares of Slovenia's Dadas plunged 53.05 percent on Monday in what traders described as "panic selling" as investors dumped the stock amid mounting fears the group's brokerage arm may be prohibited from trading.
The financial consultancy's shares tumbled 14,478 tolars to close at 12,811, dragging down the Ljubljana bourse's blue-chip SBI index five percent to a new all-time low of 893.88.

"For more than two weeks there was no information on how the case of Dadas has been developing therefore owners of Dadas shares must be losing nerves and are selling in panic," said Danilo Grasic, a trader of bank Creditanstalt.
"They prefer to sell shares at a loss than not to be able to sell them at all," he added.

Slovenia's Securities Market agency in March initiated procedures to ban brokerage Dadas from trading, claiming it was rigging the prices by trading among its affiliated companies. The brokerage is owned by listed financial consultancy Dadas.
Since then shares of Dadas have tumbled 95 percent, pulling the index down as much as 42 percent.
Traders said new information on the Dadas crisis was hard to come by, and the market watchdog agency said it would not comment on the case until it was closed.
"There may be some insider information involved in today's fall because from the information we have it cannot be explained," said Nina Jarc, a trader of bank Nova Ljubljanska banka.
The uncertainty over Dadas' prospects has dealt a heavy blow to the Slovenian bourse's attempts to attract more foreign capital to the ex-Yugoslav's nascent financial market.

Foreigners face a host of legal and bureaucratic obstacles if they want to invest in Slovenia. The government has promised to enact new legislation soon, but so far no new proposals have reached parliament.
